dish: arabiki (coarse-ground) soba and oroshi soba from buckwheat stone-milled in-house each day
n: Sobakiri Tenshō (そば切り 天笑, Hirakata)
w: Hirakata soba house that stores domestic buckwheat on site and stone-mills only the day's need; a Tabelog Soba WEST Hyakumeiten 2025 pick, and Mapple's Hirakata–Katano gourmet guide calls it a nationally known shop.

dish: shina soba: clear chicken-and-seafood double broth with three salts, chicken rare chāshū and scallop oil
n: Menya Shiki (麺ゃ しき, Moriguchi)
w: Residential-street ramen shop by Tanimachi-line Moriguchi Stn, known for its chicken rare chāshū; a Tabelog Ramen OSAKA Hyakumeiten pick (2023–2025) and profiled in Ramen Walker's 'Ramen no Jikan desu yo' column.

dish: thin-skinned, crisp-fried mini gyōza (8 per plate) with beer — the only things on the menu
n: Marushō Gyōza-ten Honten (丸正餃子店 本店, Daitō)
w: Gyōza-only shop founded 1969 near JR Suminodō, reservation-only and famous for diners ordering four or five plates each; on Time Out Osaka's 'Higashi-Ōsaka 27 must-go restaurants' (Kita-Kawachi) and Rurubu's spot guide.

dish: 'udon no tessa' — thin-rolled udon eaten like fugu sashimi with momiji-oroshi and ponzu
w: A 'drinking' udon house with obanzai sets and sake snacks alongside its signature udon tessa; on Time Out Osaka's 'Higashi-Ōsaka 27 must-go restaurants' and a Tabelog Udon WEST Hyakumeiten pick (2020, 2024).

dish: Amanozake — the revived 'sōbō-shu' temple sake of Amano-san Kongō-ji, favoured by Sengoku warlords; tastings at the brewery shop and lunch at its 'Tenkū' restaurant
n: Saijō Gōshi Gaisha — Amanozake brewery (西條合資会社 天野酒, Kawachinagano)
w: Brewery founded 1718 that in 1971 recreated the monks' sake of nearby Amano-san Kongō-ji; production capped at ~70,000 bottles, winter brewery tours. Featured by OSAKA-INFO and Rurubu.

dish: dry Delaware-grape Kawachi wine tasting after a self-guided tour of the cellar and production line
n: Kawachi Wine Kan (河内ワイン館, Habikino)
w: Family winery of ~90 years in the Habikino grape hills, Osaka's historic wine country; tours, tastings and make-your-own-label sessions. Covered by OSAKA-INFO (spot page and its Habikino winery-crawl feature) and Rurubu.
